title: Ireland – Construction work – RFT 02/26/GM - Works Contractor and PSCS for ATU Dublin Road EEDPP2 Energy Retrofit at Atlantic Technological University at the Galway City Campus
description: Atlantic Technological University (ATU) is seeking suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake an energy retrofit project at its Galway City Dublin Road Campus. The project comprises the retrofit of approximately 4,425m² of the original 1972 building and forms part of the Higher Education Authority (HEA) and Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI) funded Energy Efficiency and Decarbonisation Pathfinder Project (EEDPP2). The works include building fabric upgrades, roof and window replacement, ventilation improvements, lighting and controls upgrades, and the installation of a medium-temperature air-source heat pump, with existing gas boilers retained for peak demand and backup. The project aims to improve energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, extend the building's operational life, enhance occupant comfort, increase the use of renewable technologies, and achieve a minimum B1 BER rating. The existing building is a reinforced concrete framed structure currently served by the campus central heating system and a combination of natural and mechanical ventilation systems.

This IMPQQ competition aims to identify and shortlist highly qualified electrical contractors with proven electrical expertise and experience in Low Voltage (LV) electrical systems for light rail or heavy rail infrastructure, specifically in the design, installation, testing, commissioning, and compliance of railway electrical systems at LV level. title: Technical Assistance to Embed Renewable Integration in Madagascar Mining Permits
description: La description de l'appel d'offres ainsi que les documents de soumission sont également disponibles en français. Veuillez consulter les pièces jointes pour plus d'informations. Following the reopening of mining permits in 2026, Madagascar has an opportunity to shape how new mining investments source power. While mining and environmental regulations are in place, renewable energy integration is not yet embedded within licensing and permitting requirements. The assignment will support the Government of Madagascar to design, adopt and implement a Green Mining Energy Framework that embeds renewable energy requirements into mining licensing, environmental permitting and ESIA processes. Key outputs include a diagnostic and design options package, a Green Mining Energy Framework and supporting guidance for government adoption, and an implementation and compliance package with templates, monitoring tools and capacity-building support. The project aims to reduce future diesel dependence in the mining sector and support lower-emission mining development in Madagascar. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk

title: Unlocking Commercial and Industrial Captive Renewable Energy in Uganda: Market Sizing and Regulatory Reform
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to Uganda's Electricity Regulatory Authority (ERA). Uganda's electricity sector is predominantly powered by renewable energy and demand is growing rapidly. However, uptake of commercial and industrial (C&I) captive renewable energy remains limited due to regulatory gaps, insufficient market data, and barriers to investment. This is particularly significant given the growing role of behind-the-meter renewable energy as a means of reducing diesel reliance, improving energy security, and supporting economic growth. The assignment will support ERA, in partnership with the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development (MEMD) and electricity distributors UEDCL, WENRECO and KIS, to strengthen the enabling environment for C&I captive renewable energy. The work will establish an evidence base on market demand, existing captive generation and grid capacity, review Uganda's regulatory framework and international best practice, and develop targeted regulatory and market-enabling solutions. Key outputs are expected to include recommendations for a mid-tier regulatory framework, updated settlement and implementation guidance, standardised commercial documentation, and financing pathways to improve project bankability. The project aims to increase private-sector investment in captive renewable energy, accelerate deployment, reduce dependence on diesel generation, and strengthen Uganda's energy security and grid resilience. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk

Centralized Management & Endpoint Access: Control Center Server and Managed Device subscriptions (CCMDS/CCSVS Series) and Trusted Thin Client (TTC) Distribution Console, End User Device (EUD), and Network Resource licenses (10251 Series). Collaboration & Security Plugins: Everfox Information eXchange (DSIXTL1PU), Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Extended Lifecycle Support (ELS) nodes, and McAfee-integrated Virus Scanning Plug-Ins (2070VSP Series). Form, Fit, and Function: Software must execute native cross-domain security filtering and multi-level desktop access without requiring modification to existing agency security classification boundary policies. B. HARDWARE APPLIANCES AND HARDWARE MAINTENANCE Data Diode Appliances: Fiber-optic hardware-enforced one-way data transfer appliances (FDD10G Series) including annual hardware warranty and associated software maintenance. Cross-Domain Access (CDA) & Verifier Hardware: G2CI Cross Domain Access V2 custom hardware and hardware maintenance (1079H-CDA Series) and High-Speed Verifier turnkey appliances (HSVT Series). Form, Fit, and Function: Hardware units must conform to standard 19-inch rack-mount form factors, interface with existing fiber-optic distribution fabrics, and satisfy DoD physical separation and emissions containment standards. C. SPECIALIZED ENGINEERING AND TECHNICAL SERVICES Direct Tier-3/4 Engineering Support: Dedicated Junior, Mid-level, and Senior Product Engineers (5000/5001/5002-CDA Series) possessing relevant security clearances to provide on-site/remote deployment, complex troubleshooting, and integration. Training and Operational Travel: Basic and advanced CDA system administration training (40003-CDA Series) and associated travel (PS-TRAV-CDA) in support of mission locations. description: THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT PAY NOR REIMBURSE ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH RESPONDING TO THIS REQUEST. THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. This is a "REQUEST FOR INFORMATION" only. This Sources Sought Notice is for informational and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government. This notice is intended strictly for market research. This is not a Request for Proposal or an announcement of a solicitation, and no solicitation package exists at this time. Your responses will be used solely for market research purposes of the Government. The Government will not pay for any materials provided in response to this notice and submittals will not be returned to the sender. Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. Responses to this Sources Sought must be in writing. The James J. Peters VA Medical Center, 130 West Kingsbridge Rd, Bronx, NY 10468, has a requirement for construction services. Project Number 526-21-105 Replace Fire Alarm System. The layout is a campus with 14 buildings located on approximately 30 acres and over 1 million square feet of floor space. The existing fire alarm system is original to the new building construction circa 1980. The intent of this project is to install a new parallel fire alarm system in accordance with current NFPA and VA requirements and then once the new system is accepted remove the existing system and repair all walls, ceilings and equipment, etc. as necessary. Provide all labor, material, equipment, and supervision to perform the following: Install a new fire alarm system parallel to the existing system. This includes all new conduits and boxes, fiber optics, wiring, devices, control panels, annunciators, etc. Temporarily mount the new panels and annunciators above the existing so the new system can be tested for full and proper operation while the existing system remains operational. The following locations and equipment will primarily remain and be used as part of the new system: Building 100 Sterile Processing in Wing GA, Emergency Department in Wing 1C, Mental Health in Wing 6C. Fisher Houses 1 and 2. New control panels and communications to the control panel in Building 107 are required, existing equipment to remain but some new devices are added to bring up to code. After initial testing and acceptance of the new system, move the new panels and annunciators into the existing cabinets or boxes and relocate wiring. Remove all the old conduits and boxes, fiber optics and wiring, devices, control panels and annunciators, etc. Repair all walls, ceilings and other architectural features damaged from the installation of the new system and removal of the old. Refer to the design drawings, specification and acquisition package details. Refer to 01 00 00 General Requirements for a more detailed statement of bid. The magnitude of this project is between $10,000,000.00 and $20,000,000.00. The NAICS Code is 238210 "Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors", with a size standard of $19M. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement to include bonding capacity which shall be considered by the James J. Peters VA Medical Center. Please include the socio-economic status of your business. This is not a solicitation. If there is sufficient interest, a solicitation shall be posted on SAM.gov. Please send all inquiries to: Akkil.Kurian@va.gov by 12:00 EST Monday, September 21, 2026. Phone calls will not be accepted.

title: Request for Information (RFI) Obtaining Food Franchise Rights in Washington, DC - Northern Capital Region (NCR)
description: Request for Information (RFI) : Obtaining Food Franchise Rights in Washington, DC - Northern Capital Region (NCR) The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to gather detailed input from qualified organizations regarding the requirements, processes, and opportunities associated with obtaining food franchise rights within the Northern Capital Region (NCR), Washington, DC. Organizations responding to this RFI are requested to provide all relevant documentation, points of contact, marketing materials, and procedural information. This RFI is for planning and informational purposes only and does not obligate the Government to pursue any further action or future solicitation. Direct Engagement Model � Industry Feedback Requested In addition to information on obtaining food franchise rights generally, the FBI is specifically interested in understanding the feasibility and attractiveness of a direct-engagement model, in which the FBI would contract or otherwise arrange directly with individual food franchise brands (rather than through a single master food-service contractor) to provide food service operations within the J. Edgar Hoover Building (JEH), Washington, DC. What the FBI should understand about this model: Typical franchise agreement structures, term lengths, and capital investment requirements (buildout, equipment, branding) when a franchisor/franchisee operates within a federal government-controlled facility rather than a traditional commercial or retail location Licensing, royalty, and territory considerations that may apply or require modification for a single-tenant government building Food safety, supply chain, and operational standards the franchise would need to meet or adapt to operate within a secure federal facility Any precedent for franchise operations within federal buildings, military installations, or other access-controlled environments, and lessons learned from those arrangements All responses must be submitted to: Ms. McKenzie P. Bucher, mpbucher@fbi.gov Mr. Tom Teets, twteets@fbi.gov Please provide all requested information no later than September 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM EDT.

title: Remedial Investigation and Action at 16 AOCs at Annette Island, AK
description: The FAA has a requirement for engineering services necessary to perform remedial investigation (RI), and remedial action (RA) activities at multiple Environmental Cleanup (ECU) Program sites and areas of concern (AOCs), at 16 different AOCs, at the former Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Station on Annette Island Reserve, Alaska. Special Considerations: - This project will be performed on the Annette Island Reserve which is under the authority of the Metlakatla Indian Community (MIC). Interested vendors must have had experience in the last 10 years with the regulations of the Metlakatla Indian Community Environmental Council as well as, experience working within the Metlakatla Indian Community policies for worker and business permits, as well as materials purchase. - MIC requires all visitors to apply for a visitor permit. Visitors who will be in the community for longer than two weeks will need to apply for a residency permit. - All excavation backfill material must be purchased from MIC. No organic materials, including seed mixes, can be brought to the island. - Global positioning system (GPS) service and telecommunications are unavailable in many areas on the Metlakatla Peninsula. Satellite communications, mobile GPS antenna stations, walkie-talkies, and/or other technology resources may be needed to verify target locations, allow for communications across Contractor teams and with FAA representatives, and ensure safety of the field team. - Most sites are historical in nature and no longer serve to support FAA�s National Airspace System (NAS). Most sites were abandoned and/or demolished by the FAA in the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s. While significant clearing occurred at many of the target sites in 2023 and 2024, the Contractor should anticipate that considerable overgrowth (mostly alder and brush) or new growth is present at these sites. - The Contractor must abide by all applicable laws, codes, regulations, and guidance, and is required to perform all work in full compliance with federal, state (as applicable outside Annette Island), and local laws, codes, and regulations. The Contractor must ensure that all activities executed by their personnel, subcontractors, and suppliers are in full compliance with said laws, codes, regulations, and guidance. Any incident of noncompliance must immediately be brought to the attention of the FAA CO. Nothing in this SOW relieves the Contractor of their responsibility to comply with all applicable laws and regulations. - Prior projects encountered multiple issues due to the logistics of getting sample shipments off Annette Island and onto Gravina Island to be transported to the laboratory. The weather, airplane schedules, ferry schedules, staffing reductions and freight office closures at Alaska Airlines, can all impact the transportation of sample shipments. The 200mg/kg concentration for the MIC cleanup level for DRO and RRO makes the use of a PID/FID to screen excavations for boundary obtainment difficult. The matrix interference from organic materials, obtaining reliable usable analytical results to determine if an excavation has reached its boundary has been difficult to obtain in a reasonable timeframe. At times the laboratory data has not been usable due to matrix interference, holding time exceedance, or turnaround time delays. Summary Statement of Work: - The Contractor must submit a Work Plan that describes the Contractor's detailed approach for the performance of this contract. The work plan must be based upon this SOW. The Contractor shall review the two most recent reports for work performed for the FAA and assume that the same quality will go into the work plan. - The FAA expects that the Contractor will encounter heavy vegetation in the study areas. Old growth vegetation (assumed for purposes of this SOW as trees having a diameter of 18 inches or more at chest height) may also be encountered. If such trees are found to be present at any of the work sites, the Contractor shall coordinate with FAA and MIC to have important old growth specimens tagged. All tagged trees will be protected to the maximum extent practicable. Nevertheless, FAA expects that the Contractor will make all efforts necessary to complete the scoped activities and objectives while protecting old growth vegetation. - Clearing of vegetation is expected to the extent necessary to fully evaluate the areas of interest pursuant to this SOW. The Contractor shall use a mulching mower, brush mulcher, or similar equipment to avoid the need to haul/dispose downed vegetation. - A navigation aid outage will not be required to perform the SOW at these sites. - For all excavation confirmation laboratory samples, the Contractor shall perform Silica Gel Cleanup (SGCU) of samples by the laboratory as part of the analytical process in accordance with ADEC�s Technical Memorandum-21-001 Biogenic Interference and SGCU (December 22, 2021) to distinguish petrogenic contaminant sources from biogenic conditions. - The Contractor shall select a laboratory and processes capable of achieving sufficiently low MDLs to allow for direct comparison of analytical results to relevant CULs. - There is a discontinuous peat layer at most sites. The peat is saturated with petroleum. The peat layer when encountered and determined to be contaminated will be excavated and disposed of off island. The peat needs to be removed to help achieve reductions in the groundwater concentrations over time. - Prior investigations found that the petroleum contamination was primarily found in the top 1 to 2 feet of the AOCs, trapped in the muskeg and the top several inches of the clay layer under the muskeg. The FAA assumes that the sites will be excavated from the current edge of the pad outward and downward until extents of the petroleum contamination are found. - Prior projects encountered multiple issues due to the logistics of getting sample shipments off Annette Island and onto Gravina Island to be transported to the laboratory. The weather, airplane schedules, ferry schedules, staffing reductions and freight office closures at Alaska Airlines, can all impact the transportation of sample shipments. In order to better understand the market for this potential requirement, the FAA requests the following information from interested Small Businesses: 1. Name of Company (the resultant Prime contractor that may ultimately be awarded the subsequent contract) 2. Address 3. Point of Contact name, email address and telephone number 4. UEI Number 5. Relevant experience on similar projects within the last five years. Please provide specific contract numbers, contact names and email information to support claimed capabilities. Please submit your capability statement and the above information to Sonia.o.holguin@faa.gov no later than September 21, 2026 at 1200 Central Daylight Savings Time. Failure to respond to this pre-solicitation will preclude a Contractor�s ability to receive a copy of the future solicitation. Limit complete responses to no more than five pages. Information will not be released; however, mark PROPRIETARY on all documents submitted, as applicable.

title: Large Capacity Nonhuman Primate Cage and Rack Washer
description: This is a Notice of Intent notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Division of Veterinary Resources (DVR) within the National Institute of Health (NIH), Office of Research Services (ORS) requires the procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, and training associated with the replacement of the existing Tecniplast large-capacity nonhuman primate cage and rack washer supporting nonhuman primate housing operations at the NIH main campus, Bethesda, Maryland with minimal disruption to ongoing animal care activities. DVR requires replacement of an end-of-life cage and rack washer that supports nonhuman primate (NHP) housing operations. The existing unit, manufactured by the same company that manufactures the proposed replacement system, has been in continuous service for approximately twenty (20) years and has exceeded its expected service life. The unit is experiencing increasingly frequent failures, resulting in elevated maintenance costs, operational disruptions, and material risk to research continuity. The replacement system shall provide high-capacity, pass-through washing and sanitization for NHP cages, transport equipment, racks, feeders, enrichment devices, and ancillary husbandry equipment and shall support daily cage-wash operations. All products provided under this award must support compliance with the Animal Welfare Act (AWA), Public Health Service Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, AAALAC International Accreditation standards and Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) requirements. This is a Notice of Intent; the National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to negotiate a sole source contract for the Tecniplast USA model Atlantis EVO XL with: TECNIPLAST USA, INC. 1345 Enterprise Dr. West Chester, PA 19380-5964 Unique Entity Identifier (UEI): QHF3J4MS24H4 The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302.1(b)(1)(i) �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services will satisfy agency Requirements.�, no substitutions possible. Since the intent is to procure this on a sole source basis, no solicitation will be posted to Contract Opportunities, https://www.sam.gov. REQUIREMENT: The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, and transportation necessary to deliver, assemble, install, commission, and validate a complete and operational large-capacity cage and rack washer system at the designated DVR NHP facility location at the NIH main campus in Bethesda, Maryland. Minimum performance requirements include: Equipment: Commercial-grade, pass-through cage and rack washer with clean and dirty side barrier operation; stainless steel construction; dual interlocked tempered-glass pass-through doors with inflatable gasket system; capacity for large NHP cages, racks, transport carts, feeders, and ancillary equipment; steam-heated operation; dedicated wash and rinse circuits; separate alkaline and acid wash tanks; automated detergent dosing; tool-free self-cleaning filtration; multiple oscillating wash arm assemblies; chamber lighting; and emergency stop devices accessible from both sides. The system must exhaust through the facility's existing HVAC system and achieve a processing cycle time of approximately 20 minutes for large NHP rack loads. Controls and Monitoring: Touchscreen operator interface with multi-level password-protected controls; remote diagnostics capability; utility monitoring and consumption tracking; data logging and export functionality; Ethernet connectivity; self-start or scheduled operation functionality; and alarm monitoring and troubleshooting. Utilities: 480V/60Hz/3-phase electrical service; steam heating; domestic water supply; facility drainage connection; exhaust integration with the facility's existing HVAC system (no independent exhaust pathway or roof penetration); temperature-controlled wastewater discharge; and pH-controlled wastewater discharge. Installation and Commissioning: Coordination with DVR and ORF personnel; pre-installation site survey; equipment delivery, assembly, installation, and utility connection; startup and commissioning; operational testing documentation; Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) verifying installation, operational performance, utility and control functionality, alarm operation, wash cycle performance, and documentation delivery. Equipment shall not be considered accepted until all SAT deficiencies are corrected. Training: Onsite training for DVR personnel covering equipment operation, routine and preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, safety features, emergency procedures, and control system reporting. Training materials to be provided electronically. Warranty: Minimum two-year manufacturer warranty covering parts, labor, travel, and technical support from date of successful commissioning and acceptance, including remote technical support and onsite service when required. Required Deliverables: Equipment submittal package; shop drawings and utility requirements; Operations and Maintenance Manuals; Preventive Maintenance Schedule; Startup and Commissioning Report; Site Acceptance Test Report; Training Documentation; and Warranty Documentation. DVR�s SPECIFIC REQUIRMENTS: DVR has two mission-essential facility-driven requirements: HVAC-Integrated Exhaust Compatibility: The current NIH DVR nonhuman primate cage washroom was designed and constructed with the cage and rack washer exhausting through the building's existing HVAC system. This infrastructure configuration does not include a dedicated roof exhaust penetration or independent exhaust duct pathway for the cage wash equipment. Processing Cycle Time: The existing cage and rack washer operates at a processing cycle time of approximately 45 minutes per load. DVR has determined this to be operationally inefficient and inadequate to support current NHP husbandry throughput requirements without scheduling constraints and delays that adversely affect daily animal care operations. DVR has established a maximum processing cycle time of approximately 20 minutes as a minimum performance requirement for the replacement system. This cycle time is necessary to process the required daily volume of NHP cage wash loads within the operational constraints of the cage washroom and DVR staffing schedules, and to restore the operational efficiency degraded by the current aging unit. Market Research (Market Research Report and Acquisition Plan, separately documented) for the replacement of the large capacity and wash rack for NHP, full and open competition, vendor neutral, performance based salient features, yielded multiple commercial manufacturers (Tecniplast USA, Getinge USA, STERIS Corporation (Amsco), Allentown Inc., Alternative Design Manufacturing and Supply and others) with established product lines of large-capacity, pass-through cage and rack washer systems designed for laboratory animal facility environments. All identified vendors offer systems that generally meet the baseline performance characteristics common to this equipment category, including pass-through barrier design, stainless steel construction, steam heating, dual wash tanks, automated detergent dosing and touchscreen controls, remote diagnostics and 480V/3-phase electrical compatibility. However, the systems (Tecniplast USA, excepted) require a dedicated, independent exhaust pathway terminating at the building exterior, typically via a roof penetration. Installing a dedicated roof exhaust for an alternative unit in the existing NIH facility would require significant structural modifications, including penetration of the roof assembly, addition of dedicated ductwork through finished building spaces, and associated mechanical and structural engineering work. These modifications would result in substantial additional cost to the Government, extended construction time

title: Basic Ordering Agreement for Steel
description: SOLICITATION EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 1. THREE-STEP PROCUREMENT FRAMEWORK The Government will procure raw metal stock and components requirements utilizing a three-step process: Step One (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation): A separate Pre-solicitation Notice will not be issued; this synopsis is combined with the solicitation on SAM.gov in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.6. Individual order-level Request for Quotes (RFQs) under this Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) will be competed exclusively within the qualified pool and will not be synopsized, ensuring rapid execution. Clauses are in effect through FAC 2026-01. The primary NAICS code is 331110 (Iron and Steel Mills and Ferroalloy Manufacturing; Size Standard: 1,500 employees). Other codes are listed in Attachment 001 - Purchase Description, and the Product Service Code is 9515 (Plate, sheet, strip, foil, and leaf). Step Two (Master BOA Execution): The BOA Request for Proposal (RFP) will be released once for qualifications. The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors whose proposals are compliant with Section L and rated "Acceptable" under Section M. BOAs are valid for up to five (5) years. NOTE: This RFP is the only opportunity to obtain a raw metal stock and components BOA. Proposals will not be accepted or executed at any other time. If a contractor wishes to participate in any future raw metal stock and component orders, they must respond to this initial RFP. Step Three (Order-Level Competition): As recurring supply needs arise, the PCO will issue competitive, order-level RFQs to the BOA pool. To participate, contractors must hold an active master BOA as of the RFQ closing date. Orders will result in individual, competitive Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contracts (Orders) under FAR 16.703. 2. SCOPE Contractors will provide commercial products supporting the following CONUS sites including but not limited to: Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA) Letterkenny Munitions Center (LEMC) Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA) Tooele Army Depot (TEAD) McAlester Army Ammunition Plant (MCAAP) Joint Manufacturing and Technology Center (JMTC) Tank-Automotive and Armaments Command (TACOM) 3. SUBCONTRACTING FLEXIBILITY Offerors must demonstrate technical capability within the scope of Attachment 001: Product Description. Capability may be achieved with or without subcontractors. In Step Three order-level proposals, contractors are not bound to the subcontractors proposed in Step Two but must propose resources necessary to perform each individual order. 4. BASIS FOR AGREEMENT EXECUTION The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors with compliant proposals (Section L) rated "Acceptable" (Section M). NOTE: The Government reserves the right to waive the Compliance Review if in its best interest. The Government intends to execute BOAs on initial proposals without discussion. It reserves the right to negotiate if in its best interest but will only do so with offerors whose proposals do not contain significant informational deficiencies. LEGAL NOTICE: This master BOA process is not a competitive acquisition; the source selection procedures of FAR Part 15 do not apply. No pricing is requested or evaluated at this stage. Execution of a BOA does not constitute a contract or guarantee future orders. SECTION B � CONTRACT LINE-ITEM NUMBERS (CLINS) CLINs will be established at the order level for administrative categorization. SECTION C � EXECUTION BUSINESS RULES 1. GENERAL RULES The ordering period shall not exceed five (5) years from initial execution (DFARS 216.703(c)). Each BOA will be formally reviewed by the PCO annually (FAR 16.703(c)(2)) and revised as necessary. BOAs shall be changed only by modifying the agreement itself, not by individual orders. Modifications do not apply retroactively to active orders. Prior to the annual review, the PCO will confirm in writing if the contractor wishes to maintain the agreement. Either party may elect not to renew. The Government may cancel the BOA at any time if in its best interest. Only the Army Contracting Command�Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA) is authorized to execute, modify, or perform annual reviews of these master BOAs. Other DoD activities may place orders under these BOAs with ACC-RIA approval. 2. STEP TWO EXECUTED BOAS (QUALIFICATION PHASE) Offerors must demonstrate technical capability by filling out Attachment 001- Purchase Description by answering �Yes� to the items that can be completed and �No� to the items that cannot be completed by offeror. The purchase description at the order level will include but is not limited to the list found in Attachment 001- Purchase Description. 3. STEP THREE ORDER REQUESTS (ORDERING PHASE) Order competitions are limited to active master BOA holders. Order performance periods will be established in each order and remain valid through completion, even if they extend beyond the master BOA's 5-year term. Specific evaluation criteria (e.g., Price-Only, LPTA, or Tradeoff) will be identified in each order�s RFQ. Detail purchase descriptions requirements will be provided at the order level. All orders will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). Work shall not begin until the order is awarded. Business size standards and Non-Manufacturer Rule compliance will be certified and monitored at the order level. Offerors are required to provide pricing catalogs at the order level. SECTION H � SPECIAL CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS 1. CYBERSECURITY MATURITY MODEL CERTIFICATION (CMMC) Conditional Self-Assessment: To be eligible for award, and to remain eligible for orders, the contractor must maintain at least a conditional CMMC Level 2 Self-Assessment in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) at award. Maintenance: Failure to maintain this status will result in immediate restriction from participating in order RFQs, inability to exercise options, and potential removal from the raw metal stock and components BOA. Flow-Down: Subcontractor CMMC requirements (ranging from non-applicable to Level 2) will be defined in individual order solicitations. Primes are solely responsible for subcontractor compliance. 4. SUBCONTRACTING LIMITS AND THE NON-MANUFACTURER RULE (NMR) Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14): Primes must perform at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing (excluding materials) for supply orders. title: Design-Build of a Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) Trailer
description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) intends to award a single-award, Firm-Fixed-Price, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) systems. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a contract vehicle for the design, engineering, manufacturing, integration, testing, and production of trailer-based mobile command post systems capable of supporting FBI command, control, communications, and computer (C4) operations. The Tier II MCPV requirement consists of a custom-integrated gooseneck trailer system and, when ordered, a compatible Class 4 prime hauler vehicle. The MCPV Trailer shall provide a mobile operational environment supporting mission communications, networking, workspace, power generation and distribution, environmental control, equipment racks, audio/visual capabilities, RF and satellite connectivity provisions, security systems, and integration of Government-furnished and Contractor-furnished mission equipment. The contract will include a First Article requirement. The Contractor shall design, manufacture, integrate, test, and obtain Government approval of an initial MCPV Trailer configuration prior to production quantities. The approved First Article configuration will establish the production baseline for subsequent MCPV Trailer systems. The Government anticipates ordering approximately thirteen (13) MCPV trailer systems and associated prime hauler vehicles over the contract ordering period; however, the Government guarantees only the minimum contract obligation identified in the solicitation. The maximum contract value shall not exceed $15,000,000.00.

description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION; not a pre-solicitation notice or solicitation for proposals/quotations. Pursuant to FAR Part 10 (Market Research), the purpose of this notice is to: (1) determine if sources capable of satisfying the agency's requirements exists, (2) determine if commercial items suitable to meet the agency's needs are available or could be modified to meet the agency's requirements, and (3) determine the commercial practices of company's engaged in providing the needed service or supply. Pursuant to FAR Part 6 and FAR Part 19, competition and set-aside decisions may be based on the results of this market research. This notice in no way obligates the Government to any further action. The US Coast Guard, Surface Forces Logistic Center, Alameda CA is seeking contractors interested in providing Maintenance and Repair Services with USCGC HATCHET (WLIC 75309) with USCG 68B BARGE (68019) FY27 DRYDOCK AVAILABILITY. The US Coast Guard Cutter HATCHET (WLIC 75309) is a 75' Inland construction tender class homeported in Galveston, TX. Work list will include but is not limited: inspection, maintenance and preservation of deck equipment, cranes, winches, boat davit, anchor windlass. Cleaning and preservation of various tanks. Deck, structure, and underwater body preservation. There are approximately 88 Line Items. ***PLEASE SEE ATTACHMENT*** 1. A WLIC's design limits its use to protected and inland waters. The cutter is not crewed for continuous steaming and is normally limited to daylight transits. Due to crewing and cutter employment standards, seven days transit is the limit of crew endurance under normal operating conditions. Ten hours of transit per day is the planning factor due to crew fatigue. WLIC's have a maximum speed of 10 knots, however, environmental factors frequently limit average speed to 6.5 knots. 2. Foreseeable costs (crew lodging, messing, rental vehicles, fuel, and authorized crew travel in accordance with the Joint Travel Regulations) will be added to the pricing and will be an economic consideration for award. CUTTER�S HOMEPORT: Galveston, TX. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Contractor�s Facilities. Finally, provide documentation that shows the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. � If claiming VOSB status, provide documentation that shows the Veteran unconditionally owns 51% of the business, controls the management and daily operation, make long-term decisions for the business, and holds the highest officer position in the company that works at the business fulltime during normal working hours. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. � If claiming EDWOSB status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned by one or more women who are "economically disadvantaged", and primarily managed by an economically disadvantaged woman that make long-term decisions for the business, hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full-time during normal working hours. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. A woman is presumed economically disadvantaged if she has a personal net worth of less than $750,000.00 (with some exclusions), her adjusted gross yearly income averaged over the three years preceding the certification less than $350,000.00, and the fair market value of all her assets is less than $6 million. � If claiming Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more women, and primarily managed by one or more women that make long-term decisions for the business and hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full time during normal working hours. title: Cremation and Burial Services
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Salt Lake City Health Care System (VASLCHCS) requires a four (4) year Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for mortuary services for deceased unclaimed or indigent Veterans under VA or VA-authorized care. The Contractor shall provide professional mortuary services�including removal, preparation, storage, cremation, embalming, casketing, transportation, and confirmation of interment�for deceased unclaimed or indigent Veterans under VA or VA-authorized care in the state of Utah. Services must support delivery of deceased Veterans from the George E. Wahlen VA Medical Center or any VA-authorized care facility/location in the State of Utah (including contract nursing homes, State Veterans Nursing Homes, and other VA-authorized care locations) to the Utah Veterans Cemetery & Memorial Park at Camp Williams (17111 South Camp Williams Road, Bluffdale, Utah), the Southern Utah National Cemetery (2181 West 1600 South, Cedar City, Utah 84720), or other open state, federal, territory, or tribal Veterans cemeteries in Utah.

title: High Voltage Power Supplies (HVPS) for the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier
description: The Government has issued an Invitation for Bid (IFB) for the fabrication, pre-acceptance storage, and delivery of six (6) High Voltage Power Supply units for the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier located in Romeoville, Illinois. title: Tar Lake Superfund
description: *****Amendment 0002 ***** Amendment 0002 is being issued to respond to additional bidder inquiries, remove Davis-Bacon Construction Wage Determinations MI20260157 and MI20260158 and replace them with Davis-Bacon Construction Wage Determination MI20260043. All other terms and conditions remain UNCHANGED. ***********************Amendment 0001 ******Amendment 0001 is being issued to update the Specifications, Bid Schedule, and Scoping Statement in response to bidder inquiries received. CLIN 0007 is changed from Environmental Remediation Services to Construction. Amendment 0001 also updates the Wage Determinations found in Section L Instructions, Conditions, and Notices to Offerors or Quoters. All other terms and conditions remain UNCHANGED. ********************************************The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking a contractor for a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) environmental services contract for the Tar Lake Superfund project located in Mancelona Township, Michigan. The project includes the excavation of contaminated soil and expansion of a bio-sparge system at the Tar Lake Superfund Site in Mancelona Township, Ml. The project will involve excavation of approximately 172,500 tons of contaminated soil, backfilling with clean imported soils, installing new biosparge wells, and an approximately 160 square foot pre-engineered structure to house the biosparge system compressors. Ancillary activities include abandoning existing groundwater monitoring wells, installing new groundwater monitoring wells, installing erosion control measures, conducting a utility survey to locate existing bio-sparge system piping, confirmation soil sampling,and site restoration.

title: 88--Request for Information - Cattle Housing
description: THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The Bureau of Land Management is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify dairy farms and ranches with the capability and interest to provide temporary housing and care for cattle displaced by recent wildland fires. This RFI is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment for procurement. BACKGROUND Recent wildland fires have significantly impacted ranchers, creating an urgent need for alternative, short and long term cattle housing. The Government is seeking information on facilities that can provide safe, compliant, and reliable support for affected livestock for an estimated period of up to two years. REQUESTED INFORMATION Respondents are asked to provide detailed information regarding their capabilities, including: * Holding capacity (number and type of livestock that can be supported) * Timeframe and length of availability * Animal type preferences (steers, heifers, cows, bred cattle, bulls) * Location and description of facilities * Import requirements and required health certifications * Feed availability * Ability to provide feed onsite or support purchase/transportation * Capacity to store feed on site * Animal health requirements and standards maintained * Ability to separate or isolate cattle from existing herds as required * Veterinary support availability * Identification as a dairy farm or ranch operation ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This RFI is solely intended to gather information. No solicitation is anticipated to be issued, and no contract is anticipated to be awarded as a direct result of this notice. Information received may be shared with impacted ranchers and others, who may independently contact respondents if a need arises. The Capability statements shall be sent by email to judith_chamberlin@ios.doi.gov The capability statement must be submitted by Monday, September 21, 2026 at 1700ES

title: Design-Build of a Tier II Mobile Command Post Trailer
description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) intends to award a single-award, Firm-Fixed-Price, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) systems. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a contract vehicle for the design, engineering, manufacturing, integration, testing, and production of trailer-based mobile command post systems capable of supporting FBI command, control, communications, and computer (C4) operations. The Tier II MCPV requirement consists of a custom-integrated gooseneck trailer system and, when ordered, a compatible Class 4 prime hauler vehicle. The MCPV Trailer shall provide a mobile operational environment supporting mission communications, networking, workspace, power generation and distribution, environmental control, equipment racks, audio/visual capabilities, RF and satellite connectivity provisions, security systems, and integration of Government-furnished and Contractor-furnished mission equipment. The contract will include a First Article requirement. The Contractor shall design, manufacture, integrate, test, and obtain Government approval of an initial MCPV Trailer configuration prior to production quantities. The approved First Article configuration will establish the production baseline for subsequent MCPV Trailer systems. The Government anticipates ordering approximately thirteen (13) MCPV trailer systems and associated prime hauler vehicles over the contract ordering period; however, the Government guarantees only the minimum contract obligation identified in the solicitation. The maximum contract value shall not exceed $15,000,000.00.

title: Tar Lake Superfund
description: *****Amendment 0001 ******Amendment 0001 is being issued to update the Specifications, Bid Schedule, and Scoping Statement in response to bidder inquiries received. CLIN 0007 is changed from Environmental Remediation Services to Construction. Amendment 0001 also updates the Wage Determinations found in Section L Instructions, Conditions, and Notices to Offerors or Quoters. All other terms and conditions remain UNCHANGED. ********************************************The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking a contractor for a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) environmental services contract for the Tar Lake Superfund project located in Mancelona Township, Michigan. The project includes the excavation of contaminated soil and expansion of a bio-sparge system at the Tar Lake Superfund Site in Mancelona Township, Ml. The project will involve excavation of approximately 172,500 tons of contaminated soil, backfilling with clean imported soils, installing new biosparge wells, and an approximately 160 square foot pre-engineered structure to house the biosparge system compressors. Ancillary activities include abandoning existing groundwater monitoring wells, installing new groundwater monitoring wells, installing erosion control measures, conducting a utility survey to locate existing bio-sparge system piping, confirmation soil sampling,and site restoration.

title: Radar installation kits, management, warehousing/inventory management, and delivery of parts/materials used to overhaul multiple radar antenna systems and fire control systems.
description: Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane has a requirement to obtain individual hardware items, inspect and determine if the hardware meets the Government requirements, assemble the individual parts into system repair kits, ensure parts within the kits are packed in a manner which prevents damage to the individual parts, that marking practices result in easy identification of the kits and individual parts, the ability to pass on stringent quality requirements to suppliers, warehouse, and deliver parts/materials used to overhaul multiple radar systems and fire control systems. Requirements are in support of both US Navy and Foreign Military Sales. Delivery is required FOB Destination. NSWC Crane intends to solicit using competitive procedures and award a single five-year Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract for the compilation of new radar restoration hardware and parts kits, storage, and delivery of those kits. Forty-one (41) different parts kits are anticipated to be ordered under this contract. All kit hardware and parts are commercially available or must be manufactured according to drawings and specifications provided. title: Tar Lake Superfund
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking a contractor for a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) environmental services contract for the Tar Lake Superfund project located in Mancelona Township, Michigan. The project includes the excavation of contaminated soil and expansion of a bio-sparge system at the Tar Lake Superfund Site in Mancelona Township, Ml. The project will involve excavation of approximately 172,500 tons of contaminated soil, backfilling with clean imported soils, installing new biosparge wells, and an approximately 160 square foot pre-engineered structure to house the biosparge system compressors. Ancillary activities include abandoning existing groundwater monitoring wells, installing new groundwater monitoring wells, installing erosion control measures, conducting a utility survey to locate existing bio-sparge system piping, confirmation soil sampling,and site restoration.

description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing this Sources Sought Announcement for Construction Services for the East Bulkhead Replacement, East Boat Basin, Cape Cod Canal, Sandwich MA. This announcement is to determine interest, availability and capability of 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned and Small Business concerns for this project. The estimated construction cost is between $10,000,000 - $15,000,000. The project site is the bulkhead on the east side of the East Boat Basin of the Cape Cod Canal in Sandwich, MA. Work for this project will likely include, but not be limited to, the following: Site preparation including site demolition, excavation and fill, fencing and erosion control. Installation of approximately 960 LF of new sheet pile bulkhead and a deadmen/tieback system Partial demolition of the existing sheet piles to facilitate construction of the new bulkhead. Installation of concrete walkways, underground electric utilities, marine bollards/cleats, driveway, parking lot, trees, grass establishment, site amenities. Mobilization of equipment for construction from the water side and the land side of the bulkhead. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, small business, etc.), as well as qualifications and experience in performing the work components stated above. title: High Voltage Power Supplies (HVPS) for the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier
description: The Government has issued an Invitation for Bid (IFB) for the fabrication, pre-acceptance storage, and delivery of six (6) High Voltage Power Supply units for the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier located in Romeoville, Illinois. PROJECT INFORMATION: This is a solicitation notice for a Non-Commercial Supply contract. The project involves the fabrication of four (4) 1.5 MW and two (2) 350 kW High Voltage Power Supplies, a mandatory twelve (12) month pre-acceptance secure storage period at the contractors facility, an option for six (6) additional months of storage, and final F.o.b. Destination delivery to the operational site. SCOPE OF WORK: The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, and equipment necessary to manufacture, test, store, and deliver six (6) complete, fully functional HVPS units in strict accordance Scope of Work (SOW). These units are a critical component of the nations aquatic invasive species defense system. This will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP), IFB procurement in accordance with FAR Part 14, Sealed Bidding. The Government intends to award to the lowest priced bidder deemed responsive and responsible. title: Non- Standard Weapons (NSW)/ Commercially available M134D Miniguns, Mounts, Support Equipment, Spare Part Kits and Installation/Training Services
description: The purpose of this effort is to issue a sole source solicitation under Title 10 United Stated Code (U.S.C.) �3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1(c)(2)(i), substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition to Dillon Aero, Inc. This sole source requirement will result in a Firm Fixed Priced Indefinite Delivery Indefinite contract. The requirement for M134D Minigun weapon systems, along with associated mounting systems for various air/water/ground platforms, parts, accessories, support equipment, installation, and training for operators and maintainers. The M134D variants, including the M134D-H and M134D-M, are 7.62x51mm rotary machine guns. The Government has a need for M134D variants as they are capable of delivering precision and rapid fire on personnel and vehicle-sized (2m x 3m) materiel targets with fixed firing rates of 3,000 rounds per minute. The M134D-H is a hybrid design that utilizes titanium and skeletonized parts to offer increased weight savings of 10-20 pounds while retaining the longer service life of the steel gun. The M134D-M (marinized) variation utilizes ceramic coatings to improve corrosion resistance for use in the marine environment. Spare parts and accessories are also required for each configuration and will be incorporated into the contract. Installation and training services will be included for platform installation (air/ground/water platforms) and operator and maintainer training courses.

title: Tyndall Mess Attendant Recompete
description: This is a contract for mess attendant support services for the Berg-Liles Dining Facility which will remain under the full operational and management control of the 325th Fighter Wing Force Support Squadron (FSS), Tyndall AFB, FL. Management and operational control retained by the 325th FSS will include but is not limited to all management responsibility, oversight and decision-making authority of the day-to-day operations of the dining facility including establishing operational hours, budgeting, accounting and recordkeeping, storeroom management, and other management functions. At no time shall the contractor exercise any operational control of the dining facility in the performance of this contract. The contractor shall perform the requirements in the PWS IAW Tri-Service Food Code and conform to the professional standards identified in this contract. Furthermore, the contractor shall follow all applicable federal laws, regulations, instructions and directives as identified in the PWS. Contractor tasks include, but not limited to, the following: serving and replenishing food; cleaning interior and exterior of facilities, equipment, and utensils; maintain equipment and repair as required; preparing raw vegetables and fruits for the self-serve bars and for use by military cooks; preparing cold cuts and cheeses for the use by military cooks at the sandwich/deli bar; ensure coverage for ethnic and/or specialty food bars; make and wrap sandwiches; cut and portion pastry items and provide cashier services. In the event of a contingency the contractor may be required to provide cooks on a temporary basis to ensure continued service. The intent is to negotiate a two-phase firm fixed price purchase order with Precision Integrated Programs, LLC., to procure Crash Attenuating Seat Assemblies Structural Fabrication and Installation on an Airbus AS-332L1 Super Puma Helicopter. This service includes the following: Phase I - Manufacturing: The offeror shall manufacture all parts/placards/assemblies required for one full installation of crash attenuating seats. Phase II - Assembly and Installation: The offeror shall hold an FAA part 145 Certified Repair Station (CRS) certificate with an Airframe Class 4 rating or Super Puma helicopter limited rating. The firm fixed purchase order will be for the services provided herein. The anticipated award date is October 1, 2026. This is a sole source solicitation to Precision Integrated Programs, LLC. No other sources will be considered. This requirement is not set aside for small business.

title: Vehicle Maintenance Services
description: The purpose of this contract is to provide vehicle maintenance services for 801st Red Horse Squadron (RHS) at Tyndall AFB, FL in accordance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS) in a manner that provides a safe and serviceable vehicle fleet that is critical to the success of the Silver Flag Exercise training site. The contractor shall provide all personnel, supervision, and services necessary to ensure vehicle maintenance, vehicle fleet management, and vehicle operation functions identified in the PWS. In addition, the contractor shall provide management and administrative functions for maintaining the special/general purpose vehicle fleet, weapon systems fleet, organizational equipment, and shop equipment. Services dedicated to the duration of this contract is for a base period of twelve months plus four option years at twelve months each. The solicitation is for a commercial service and prepared in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The solicitation will result in a firm, fixed price contract. The successful contractor will be selected using Best Value Trade-Off source selection procedures, resulting in the best value for the Government. The government is holding a site visit on August 11th, 2026 at 9:00 AM CDT. More information regarding the site visit is in Attachment 03 FAR 52.212-1 Instruction to Offerors section Q. No paper copies will be issued. The applicable NAICS Code and Small Business Administration (SBA) Size Standard for this acquisition are 811111 and $9M, respectively. This acquisition will be a competitive total small business set-aside. Interested parties must express interest by 5 days prior and have all information submitted no later than 2 days prior to ensure proper processing. To be eligible for contract awards, offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Registration is accomplished via the SAM website at https://www.sam.gov.Any questions related to this pre-solicitation notice must be submitted in writing via email SrA Sarah Marip at sarah.marip@us.af.mil or SSgt Firas Aldarawcheh at firas.aldarawcheh@us.af.mil.

The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4.
